test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 16 Jun, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
How many rural households were graded based on deprivation criteria, as per Socio

Economic and Caste Census (SECC) that was concluded by the Ministry of Rural

Development in March, 2016?
solution:
The correct answer is __**8.72 crore**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• As per the Socio-Economic and Caste Census (SECC) conducted by the Ministry of Rural Development, **8.72 crore rural households** were graded based on deprivation criteria.
 
• The SECC was a significant initiative aimed at identifying households based on **economic and social deprivation parameters**.
 
• This census was concluded in **March 2016** and formed the basis for targeting beneficiaries under various social welfare schemes.
 
• The SECC categorization ensures **better targeting of subsidies and welfare programs** by identifying the most deprived households.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Socio-Economic and Caste Census (SECC):**

 
 
• The SECC was conducted in 2011, with its analysis completed later for targeted policy implementation.
 
• It aimed to collect data on multiple deprivation indicators such as housing, education level, income, and employment status.
 
 
 
• **Deprivation Criteria:**
 
 
• Households were evaluated on factors such as income, land ownership, access to education, and type of dwelling.
 
• These criteria were used to prioritize households for government schemes like housing, employment, and healthcare.
 
 
 
• **Importance:**
 
 
• The SECC data is crucial for implementing targeted welfare policies for rural development.
 
• It provides valuable insights into poverty and socio-economic challenges in India.
 
 
 
• **Ministry of Rural Development:**
 
 
• The Ministry spearheaded the SECC initiative and ensured data collection from all rural households.
 
• It is responsible for implementing rural welfare programs in India.
